idioms.gloss: To make a remark or provide information when it is inappropriate or indiscreet to do so, or when one does not have permission or the authority to do so.
To say one's thoughts aloud, particularly while also not conversing with anyone else.
To discuss one's work or (sometimes, by extension) hobby; especially, to do so in a way that only insiders would understand, is tedious or boring to the listener, or both.
To perform actions consistent with one's claims.
It is easy to make boastful or unrealistic statements which are not supported by actions or evidence.
To speak lacking expertise, authority, or knowledge; to invent or fabricate facts.
To brag; to exaggerate one's abilities or achievements.
To talk pedantically, or using excessively difficult or literary words.
To talk to someone excessively, or far more than is wanted or appreciated.
To be completely ignored or disregarded by someone, as if speaking to an inanimate object.

Used to dismiss another person's argument by indicating that one is not prepared to hear or read anything further from that person. It is often used while simultaneously holding up the hand with the palm facing the speaker.
To talk for a long duration of time, at a rapid pace without giving others a chance to speak, or to the point of tedium.
To speak glibly and persuasively; to persuade or achieve an objective with smooth talk.
To make statements that profess commitment, knowledgeability, or intended action (especially when the speaker's actual commitment, knowledge, or further action are in doubt).
To untruthfully speak of another in a belittling, deprecative, slighting manner, either in person or in absentia.
To talk nonsense.
To use profane language, especially sexual vulgarities for the purpose of arousal.
To talk badly about something.
